distance_note: Piers 68 & 70's dry-dock and ship-repair facility sits immediately north of Brookfield's tracked 28-acre Pier 70 redevelopment parcel and Crane Cove Park, outside both -- Port materials describe it as a separate 13-acre facility, closed in 2017, at the complex's northeast corner.
summary: Two Port-owned floating dry docks at Piers 68 & 70 -- Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock -- that the Port Commission declared an emergency over on 2025-12-08 after hull tears and uncontrolled ballast-tank flooding caused Dry Dock No. 2 to list. The Port is stabilizing both structures and plans to demolish and dispose of them, at a total estimated cost of $61.2M, of which about $20.0M was secured as of February 2026.

milestones.text: Port Commission authorizes Resolution 24-51 funding toward Pier 70 shipyard dry dock work; the formal supplemental appropriation ordinance was introduced later (see 2025-12 and 2026-02 entries).

Existing tears in Dry Dock No. 2's hull enlarge and new tears appear, causing uncontrolled flooding of ballast tanks; the dry dock is then found to have excessive listing on its northeast side following a rainstorm.
The Port Commission President and Executive Director declare the existence of an emergency over Dry Dock No. 2's condition.
Mayor introduces a supplemental appropriation ordinance for dry dock emergency stabilization and future demolition funding.

Port Commission receives an informational memo (Calendar Item 9A) on the dry dock emergency, the stabilization work under way (continuous pumping, reinforcing steel, stabilizing deck cranes, capped at $10,000,000), and staff's plan to advertise a demolition-services contract in summer 2026.

Capital Planning Committee reviews a supplemental memo giving the full cost picture: $61.2M total estimated cost to stabilize and dispose of Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock, of which about $20.0M was secured and about $41.2M remained pending FY2026-27 budget approval.
Port staff anticipate advertising a contract for demolition services in the summer of 2026 (staff's informal name for the underlying memo: the "Dry Dock Memorandum").

costs.what: Cap on emergency stabilization work (continuous pumping, reinforcing steel, stabilizing deck cranes) authorized under the Port's December 2025 emergency declaration

Total estimated cost to stabilize and dispose of Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock (Phase 1A stabilization $8.6M + Dry Dock No. 2 disposal $27.4M + Eureka disposal $15.7M + $9.5M contingency, per the Capital Planning Committee's Feb 2026 cost table); about $20.0M was secured as of Feb 2026, with roughly $41.2M pending FY2026-27 budget approval

facts.value: Two floating dry docks: Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock (the latter formerly USS Steadfast, AFDM-14 -- not the 1890 ferryboat Eureka preserved at Hyde Street Pier/SF Maritime NHP)

open_questions: Whether the $18.5M Port Commission Resolution 24-51 authorization (Oct 2024) is a subset of, or additional to, the $61.2M total cost figure presented in the Feb 2026 Capital Planning Committee memo is not established by the sources reviewed here.

Whether demolition will be completed "before winter storms" (a claim in an unsourced summary, not repeated in this record) is not supported by any primary source found; SFist (2026-03-05) reports it will likely be a year before the dry dock situation is resolved, and roughly $41.2M of the $61.2M total remained unfunded as of Feb 2026.
What becomes of BAE Systems' ship-repair operations at the adjacent Pier 70 shipyard once these dry docks are removed is not addressed in the sources reviewed here.
